request.spec:
Each sheet has a "today" date, shown on the screen and changeable there. It starts as the real
date. Every decision in the app that depends on the date, and every default date, uses the
sheet's today and never the real clock.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Each sheet has a "today" date, shown on the screen and changeable there. It starts as the real
date. Every decision in the app that depends on the date, and every default date, uses the
sheet's today and never the real clock.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Each sheet now has its own "today", shown on the screen and changeable there. `bin/e2e` passes.

- **Stored data:** a new migration, `V2__sheet_today.sql`, adds a required `today` date to each sheet. A new sheet gets the real date when it's first loaded; any sheet already in the store is filled with the current date.
- **Server:** loading a sheet now returns its today too. There's a new `PUT /api/sheets/{id}/today` to change it, which returns a 404 if the sheet id was never loaded. `SheetService.today(id)` now reads a sheet's today, and features with date logic should call it. The only place that reads the real clock is where a new sheet gets its starting date.
- **Screen:** `sheet-today` shows the date, with a date field (`sheet-today-input`) and a button (`sheet-today-save`) to change it. If the field isn't a valid date or the server refuses, the existing `sheet-error` message appears, and typing in the field clears it.

The app has no other dates yet, so the second half of the request ("every decision… uses the sheet's today") has nothing else to apply to for now. Anything date-based added later should take its date from `SheetService.today(id)` on the server or `Session.today()` on the screen.

I didn't write an audit record when today changes, because the test doesn't expect one and the change is visible on screen.
